response.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS high_peercorr_count FROM advancedbehavior WHERE peercorr > 0.149;

assumptions.assumption: "High" means strictly above the 0.149 cutoff (peercorr > 0.149), so a record exactly at 0.149 is not counted.
Records with a NULL peercorr are not counted, since NULL never satisfies the comparison.
High peer correlation means a positive correlation above the cutoff, so negative values are not counted.

alternatives.interpretation: The cutoff is inclusive: count records whose peer correlation is at least 0.149.
alternatives.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS high_peercorr_count FROM advancedbehavior WHERE peercorr >= 0.149;

alternatives.interpretation: High means a strong correlation in either direction: count records whose absolute peer correlation is above 0.149.
alternatives.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS high_peercorr_count FROM advancedbehavior WHERE ABS(peercorr) > 0.149;
